original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-map-flat-case}
Let
$$
\xymatrix{
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'})
\ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} &
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \ar[d]^f \\
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})
\ar[r]^g &
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules.
Assume both $g$ and $g'$ are flat.
Then there exists a canonical base change map
$$
g^*Rf_*\mathcal{F}^\bullet
\longrightarrow
R(f')_*(g')^*\mathcal{F}^\bullet
$$
in $D^{+}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})$.

final_content.statement:
Consider a **commutative** square of ringed topoi $\mathcal C'\xrightarrow{g'}\mathcal C$ over $\mathcal D'\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal D$, with vertical arrows $f':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal D'$ and $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$. Both horizontal maps $g,g'$ are assumed flat, so their pullback functors $g^*,(g')^*$ are exact and act on derived categories without additional derived-pullback notation. The assertion is **existence** of a canonical base-change morphism; it does **not** assert an isomorphism.

Let
$$
\xymatrix{
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'})
\ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} &
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \ar[d]^f \\
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})
\ar[r]^g &
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules.
Assume both $g$ and $g'$ are flat.
Then there exists a canonical base change map
$$
g^*Rf_*\mathcal{F}^\bullet
\longrightarrow
R(f')_*(g')^*\mathcal{F}^\bullet
$$
in $D^{+}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})$.
hypotheses: The displayed square of ringed topoi is commutative, with morphisms $f,f',g,g'$ in the indicated directions.
$g$ and $g'$ are **flat** morphisms of ringed topoi.
$\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a bounded-below complex of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-modules.
conclusions: There is a canonical morphism $g^* Rf_*\mathcal F^\bullet\longrightarrow R(f')_*(g')^*\mathcal F^\bullet$ in $D^+(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D'})$.
